> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `74a360f307087ca6031391273c8f8e1e216841db` — the merge of head `b1f2335b29d12e5494247d1a2bab6796da6fad8c` into base `018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 74a360f307087ca6031391273c8f8e1e216841db && git checkout 74a360f307087ca6031391273c8f8e1e216841db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895 b1f2335b29d12e5494247d1a2bab6796da6fad8c && git checkout -B drift-repro 018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895 && git merge --no-ff b1f2335b29d12e5494247d1a2bab6796da6fad8c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 018b077fbf8876c0fd5f46e66dcc551a4e74c895` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5354b160163455c1558da61a18a66c905b4a310e`
Local-runs: none

First record on this PR (stage W of #15204, the walled catalog refusal, ADR-0131 D3). Reviewed read-only: the PR body and its 19-file list (+1,196 / −29), the net diff of `5354b160` against `main` (base `45e206e4`, the three-dot diff after the two `origin/main` merges `376af552` and `d2a6934e`), card #15204's body and all 138 comments through 6114486311 (the stage-W seat note 6112750171 with its five measurement questions, the measurement report 6113821871, the seat note 6113841670 with release-cut condition (f) and the patch round, the patch-round report 6114447595, the rulings 6095027530 (#22621 → A) and the triage pointer 6070695107), ADR-0131 D3 / D4 / D7 / D11 / D13, ADR-0090 D12 and ADR-0087 (the launch-window section and the disposition addendum) as served on `main`, and on `main` the activation gate, the four REST `/meta` write doors, the dispatcher's `/meta` branch, `permission-set-clone.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`'s middleware roster, `resolve-authz-context.ts`'s rung derivation, the two re-judged test files and the ObjectQL middleware contract. `main` read at `63739521d8`, which contains the PR base.

**Gate verdicts on the head, read at 2026-10-11T22:36Z.** 42 check-runs across two workflow rounds, every one `completed`: 38 `success`, 4 `skipped` (the second round's `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`, which the first round ran green, and the two roster skips `Console Pin Gate` and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`). Nothing is pending. Green among them: `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check:system-context-census`), `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` against the merge base and the no-major guard), `TypeScript Type Check` with its four sub-gates, `Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1/3 to 3/3, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, and the five PR-form guards. No review is submitted on the PR; it is a draft, `mergeable` true, no auto-merge armed. Where a judgment below says "pinned", the pin is one of these green runs, not a local run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **The doors (brief point a).** On `main` exactly six caller-facing doors write a `position`, `permission` or `capability` item, read off the callers of `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` and of `saveMetaItem` plus the engine writers of the three tables: REST `PUT` (save), `DELETE` (reset), `POST …/publish` and `POST …/rollback` on `/meta/:type/:name`; the dispatcher's `PUT` (its `DELETE` / `POST` / `PATCH` on an item answer `405` with an `Allow` header, so it has one write door); the clone door `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone`; and the data door on `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set`, `sys_capability`. The diff adds `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` after the capability gate at every one of them: the four REST sites (`rest-server.ts` save, reset, publish, rollback, each before `resolveProtocol`), the dispatcher's `PUT` branch (before anything is read or written), the clone door (before any catalog read), and a middleware registered per catalog object. The activation door (`/security/_activation/...`) already refuses below the operator rung on `main` (`refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`) and is left alone — **right**. The data-door middleware judges `insert`, `update`, `delete`, which is the whole write vocabulary the ObjectQL middleware chain carries (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate` are the rest; no bulk or upsert operation exists), so no write verb slips past it — **right**. It is registered after the security middleware (`:2323`, which also hosts the ADR-0090 D12 delegated-admin gate) and after the position catalog refusal, before the permission-set write-through and the position write-through, so a refused write is never translated into a metadata save — **right**, and the ablation the dev reports (registration removed, six refusal pins red, controls green) is the measured form of the same claim. Engine writers that remain are `permission-set-projection.ts` (projector, `SYSTEM_CTX`), `position-environment-backfill.ts` (migration), the two write-throughs (behind the new middleware) and the registry's `registerItem` calls in `builtin-positions.ts` / `builtin-capabilities.ts` (boot declarations) — all system writes, all admitted by `isSystem`. No door is left out. Two adjacent doors I considered and judge outside D3's catalog-write set are in ③ (items 8 and 9).

2. **The predicate (brief point b).** `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` admits everything outside `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES`, admits when the posture is `undefined` or not wall-enforcing (`postureEnforcesWall` from `@objectstack/spec/security`, the activation gate's own test), admits `isSystem === true`, admits `callerPosture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`, refuses the rest — **right**. Inert under `single` and with no `tenancy` service: pinned (`meta-write-capability.test.ts`, the dispatcher's `single` and no-service controls, the dogfood `single` control where a `manage_metadata` holder who is not the platform administrator still saves a position, #22621 → A unchanged). The operator rung is the context's `posture`, which `resolve-authz-context.ts` derives through `derivePosture({ isPlatformAdmin: hasPlatformAdminGrant })`, and `hasPlatformAdminGrant` is set by exactly two routes: the configured `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` match, and the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant only while `legacyGrantAnchorRetired` is false, i.e. never under a wall. No held capability and no position name reaches it; a context carrying no rung is refused (pinned) — **right**, and it is the activation gate's `ec?.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` test verbatim. URL spellings: the predicate and `isSecurityCatalogType` fold through `canonicalMetaUrlType` from `@objectstack/spec/meta-spelling`, the one function `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:342` applies at the `saveMetaItem` boundary (`spec/src/meta-spelling/metadata-url-spelling.ts:161`, re-exported by `shared`), so `/meta/permissions/x` is judged as `permission` — **right**, pinned on the dispatcher. A registered `tenancy` service that cannot answer: on REST the read goes through `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy`, which returns `undefined` only for the never-registered brand and otherwise throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('tenancy')`, which the route's `handleRouteError` answers with the error's own status; on the dispatcher and the clone door `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` throws the same error, which is the activation gate's body moved into a named function and called from its old site — **right**: a throw is never a permit. At the data door the posture is the security plugin's one start-time read (`this.tenancyPosture`), which resolves a `tenancy` service that answers nothing to `single`; that is not a 503, and the PR body's "503, never a permit" sentence is true of the three transport doors, not of the data door. I judge it **right** nonetheless: that read is the same one that decides whether Layer 0 walls any object at all, so a deployment whose plugin reads `single` enforces no wall for this refusal to protect, and reading the posture twice through two mechanisms in one plugin would be the drift the activation gate's comment warns against. Named, not failed.

3. **The answers (brief point c).** REST `/meta` answers `403 FORBIDDEN`; the dispatcher `PUT`, the clone door and the data door answer `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. Read against `main`: each of the four REST doors' own capability refusal already answers `res.status(403).json({ error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', … } })`; the dispatcher's capability refusal is `deps.error(verdict.message, 403)`, whose code `buildApiError` derives from the status through `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` ("this transport's pinned spelling", the branch's own comment); the clone door uses the same `deps.error`; the data door throws `PermissionDeniedError`, the plugin's one refusal class. So the split is the **pre-existing per-transport envelope**, and the diff puts each new refusal in exactly the envelope the door's sibling refusal already uses — **right**. A refusal that invented a third spelling, or made the two transports agree by changing one of them, would have been the defect; neither happened. The changeset and the semantic entry name both spellings.

4. **The accept-set narrowing beyond the measured cross-tenant write (brief point d).** ADR-0090 D12's delegated scope may "optionally author environment-owned sets"; its `authorEnvironmentSets` arm lives in `delegated-admin-gate.ts` (`:906`) inside the security middleware, and admits a `sys_permission_set` write at the data door only. After this PR such a delegate under a wall passes the delegated gate and is refused by the walled middleware behind it. Within D3: **yes** — D3's rule is by rung and posture ("tenant admins cannot create or edit catalog items; the operator defines the catalog for every tenant"), a delegate is a principal below the operator rung inside one organization, and ADR-0131 is the later record. Does the changeset's FROM → TO say it: **in population terms, yes** — its data-door bullet reads "FROM admitted to any caller whose grants admit the table TO `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`", and the delegated gate is what admits the table to a delegate; **by name, no** — neither the changeset nor the semantic entry's `surface` spells `authorEnvironmentSets` or ADR-0090 D12; only the PR body's Acceptance notes do. Judged right for the verdict (the accept-set change is declared and the level is BREAKING already); the missing name is carried in ③ item 4 for the seat.

5. **Assignments and engine writes (brief point e).** `WALLED_CATALOG_OBJECT_TYPES` is exactly the three catalog objects (pinned, "assignment objects are never judged"); `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set` have no registration. Controls pinned: the walled tenant still assigns a catalog position (`walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`, both postures), still assigns a permission set through `POST /data/sys_user_permission_set` on the booted stack (dogfood, `201`), and the boot golden's assignment cases do not move. Engine writes: `isSystem` admitted at the predicate (pinned), a system `sys_position` insert admitted at the data door under a wall (pinned), the position write-through's "a system write is never translated" pin untouched, the operator saves and clones under both postures (dogfood controls, `200`). The grant-by-name door (#22863) writes `GRANT_OBJECT = 'sys_user_permission_set'` and only reads the catalog; the suggestion-confirm door is already behind `assertDeploymentAuthority` and since stage 1 writes a junction row that grants nothing — **right**.

6. **The ADR-0087 entry and the changeset (brief point f).** `18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired.ts` carries the five `SemanticMigration` fields (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`); `surface` avoids backticks as the generator requires; entries are discovered one-file-per-entry under `entries/semantic/`, and `Check Changeset` verified the id resolves and is new in the diff. The changeset: five packages at `minor` (`metadata-core`, `rest`, `runtime`, `plugin-security`, `spec`), `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on its own line, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the marker `adr-0087: registered walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired`, a FROM → TO per door, an Unchanged paragraph, and the remedy (the operator defines in Studio or a managed package; tenants assign; a custom door asks the predicate after `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`) — **right**; ② judges the levels. The dev's deviation 4 (the gate refuses a FROM → TO body beside `not-required`, so the change is `registered`) is the ADR-0087 addendum's own rule ("`no-migration-prescription` is refused by a body that carries a migration prescription") — **right**.

7. **Census row 55b and the counts (brief point g).** The regenerated counts move 124 → 129 reads, which is the five `isSystem` reads the diff adds (the predicate's input, `walledCatalogRefusal`, the dispatcher branch, the data-door middleware, the clone door); files 58 → 59 (one new file, `walled-catalog-data-door.ts`; the other four files were already anchored), symbols 106 → 109 (`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, `walledCatalogRefusal`, `createWalledCatalogDataDoorRefusal`; the dispatcher's and the clone door's reads sit in symbols already anchored), declarations 28 → 29 (the predicate's `isSystem?: boolean`), and the row's anchors name those three symbols. The arithmetic closes and `Lint & Repo Gates` holds it — **right**. The two new `scripts/adr-anchors/*.json` files anchor ADR-0131 on the predicate's file and the data door's file — **right**.

8. **The two re-judged pins (brief point g).** `position-write-through.test.ts`: the old pin "a walled posture: an organization administrator's create lands its organization row, and no definition" is the behaviour D3 refuses; the new pin asserts `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, zero rows, `saveMetaItem` not called and zero environment rows — strictly more is asserted, nothing is dropped: **the D3 refusal, not a weakening**. Its promotion pin now seeds the pre-existing row-only position with an `isSystem` insert instead of a tenant create and keeps every downstream assertion (catalog does not resolve, the metadata-door definition promotes it, `permissionSets` read back); that population is #15196 Q3 = A's, as the comment says — **right**. `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`: `REFUSAL_GOLDEN`'s "control: create a position row" was `{ ok: true }` for every scenario; `refusalGoldenFor` now overrides it to `{ ok: false, code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403 }` when `scenario.posture !== 'single'` (the `Scenario.posture` union is `'single' | 'isolated'`, so the `walled` scenario and its three variants), and leaves the assignment rows, the `reference_not_found` cases and the two built-in-row refusals untouched — **the D3 refusal, not a weakening**. `group` is not in that harness and is pinned in `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts` instead.

9. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/metadata-core` gains four exports (`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, `isSecurityCatalogType`, `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES`, `PLATFORM_OPERATOR_POSTURE`), named in the changeset's remedy; `@objectstack/runtime` gains `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` from `activation-gate.ts`, a factoring of the gate's own body whose old call site now calls it (the refusal path, the `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` wrap and the `undefined`-posture early return are byte-for-byte the same decisions) — **right**, additive, and the message strings of the activation gate are unchanged.

10. **The dispatcher reads the posture only for a catalog type** (`isSecurityCatalogType(type)` guards the `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` call) and REST's helper returns `{ allowed: true }` before the tenancy read for any other type, so a `view` or `object` save pays no tenancy read and cannot meet a tenancy 503 it did not meet before — **right**, pinned ("a type outside the catalog is not judged").
